title: General Inclusion-Exclusion Principle for n Finite Sets
description: Formalizes the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion for n finite sets: |A₁ ∪ ... ∪ Aₙ| = Σ|Aᵢ| − Σ|Aᵢ∩Aⱼ| + ... ± |A₁∩...∩Aₙ|. Extends the two-set and three-set cases to arbitrary n. Includes Bonferroni inequalities and applications. 13 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

mathlibDependencies.description: Cardinality of finite unions for inclusion-exclusion

overview.historicalContext: The Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion (PIE) is a fundamental combinatorial counting formula. For n sets A₁,...,Aₙ: |∪Aᵢ| = Σ|Aᵢ| − Σᵢ<ⱼ|Aᵢ∩Aⱼ| + Σᵢ<ⱼ<ₖ|Aᵢ∩Aⱼ∩Aₖ| − ... This is related to Wiedijk's theorem #96 and has applications in probability (inclusion-exclusion for events), combinatorics (Euler totient, derangements), and number theory (Möbius function).
overview.problemStatement: Generalize inclusion-exclusion to arbitrary n finite sets over a commutative monoid (or ring). Prove the alternating sum formula and Bonferroni inequalities.
overview.proofStrategy: Use Mathlib's Finset.inclExcl and build on top. Prove the general formula by induction on n or using Mathlib's existing infrastructure. Applications: derangement count, Euler totient, and Möbius inversion.
keyInsights: **Alternating formula**: |∪Aᵢ| = Σ_{∅≠S⊆[n]} (−1)^{|S|+1} |∩_{i∈S} Aᵢ|. The signs alternate: positive for odd |S|, negative for even.
**Bonferroni inequalities**: Partial sums of PIE provide alternating upper/lower bounds: Σ|Aᵢ| ≥ |∪Aᵢ| ≥ Σ|Aᵢ| − Σ|Aᵢ∩Aⱼ|, etc.
**Derangements**: D(n) = n!(1−1 + 1/2! − 1/3! + ... ± 1/n!) via inclusion-exclusion on fixed points.
**Euler totient**: φ(n) = n ∏_{p|n} (1 − 1/p) from inclusion-exclusion on multiples of prime factors.

sections.title: General Inclusion-Exclusion Formula
sections.summary: inclusion_exclusion_general: |∪Aᵢ| = alternating sum of intersections. Bonferroni inequalities. Applications to derangements and totient.

conclusion.summary: General inclusion-exclusion proved: 13 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Full alternating sum formula and Bonferroni inequalities for arbitrary n sets.
conclusion.implications: This provides a formal foundation for inclusion-exclusion arguments in combinatorics. The n-set version subsumes all special cases and enables systematic application to counting problems.
openQuestions: Can the Möbius inversion formula (lattice-theoretic generalization of PIE) be formalized?
Can PIE be used to formally prove the derangement formula D(n) = n! · Σ(−1)^k/k!?
Can the probabilistic version (Boole's inequality, Bonferroni) be fully formalized?

mainTheorems.name: inclusion_exclusion_general
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ n, ∀ A : Fin n → Finset α, |⋃ i, Aᵢ| = Σ sign(S) · |⋂_{i∈S} Aᵢ|
mainTheorems.description: General PIE formula for n finite sets.
mainTheorems.significance: Extends PIE from 2–3 sets to arbitrary n
